biodiversity_overview.text: 3,292 GBIF occurrence records for 34 tracked species are attributed to Andaman & Nicobar, spanning 1875-2026.
3,131 of these records (95.1%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Actinopterygii 12, Magnoliopsida 8, Aves 7, Testudines 2, Mammalia 2, Amphibia 1, Squamata 1, Elasmobranchii 1.

threatened_species.text: 3 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Cuckoo (1,981), Indian White-eye (587), Indian Pond-heron (325), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (82), Bulletwood (75).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 36 in 2016 to 52 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 11.73% of Andaman & Nicobar's area (77 areas intersect the state).
1.3% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (40 of 3,131); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Green Turtle (0.40), Indian Ash Tree (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Leatherback (0.31), Bulletwood (0.30).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Andaman & Nicobar (equal-weight reference): cell near 11.625N 92.625E (overall rank 177, median rank across weightings 192); cell near 12.375N 92.625E (overall rank 223, median rank across weightings 235); cell near 11.625N 93.375E (overall rank 274, median rank across weightings 279).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 6,859 km2 (90.57% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

184.4 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (2.69% of the 2000 extent; 0.32% in 2015-2024, rank 22 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2005 (35.5 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.12% of land and population density is 52.5 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
6% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
